Subject: Globex latency & throughput benchmark - next steps

Hi Max / Elena - great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Recap: you’re running a user-facing summarization pipeline with 99% of requests <512 tokens and a small tail to 2k tokens. Primary goals are p95 < 200ms for interactive flows and sustained tokens/sec for batch summarization.
- Primary evaluation asks: end-to-end p95/p99, steady-state tokens/sec at target concurrency, and variability at different batching policies. You also flagged competitive comparison to your current hyperscaler inference API (we’ll call that “Hyperscaler API” in notes).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a representative prompt set (anonymized) + target throughput (RPS) and any sequence-length distribution you have.
2) Our SRE/bench team will run an A/B test: Redwood (quantized and unquantized variants) vs Hyperscaler API using identical request workload. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail jitter, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M-tokens.
3) Initial run: 24-48 hours of steady-state tests, then a focused peak-run to capture tail behavior.

Can you drop the sample prompt set and an example payload (anonymized) into a shared folder? If helpful, we can also run a short smoke test this week before the full A/B.

I’ll loop in Rishi (bench lead) and Lauren (AE) to propose configs.

Thanks - Marissa

Looping in bench details - early bench notes and proposed test config below. I also attached the summary CSV and a short PDF with the baseline A/B config.

Quick summary of initial smoke runs (local perf lab, representative subset):
- Redwood (quantized Llama-2-70B int8, continuous batching enabled, kv-cache warm): p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 280ms, steady tokens/sec ~ 42k at 16 concurrent streams (avg seq len ~320).
- Redwood (fp16, no quant): p95 ~ 150ms, p99 ~ 220ms, tokens/sec ~ 55k at same concurrency.
- Hyperscaler API (public endpoint, comparable model family): p95 ~ 260ms, p99 ~ 420ms, tokens/sec ~ 28k.

Notes: the Hyperscaler runs show heavier tail due to their per-request cold-start and smaller sustained batching window in their managed endpoint. Our continuous batching + prefix KV caching reduces per-token latency in sustained workloads.

Proposed full A/B test config (what we will run for the 24-48h):
- Workload: 2k samples from Globex (you provided), replay at target RPS: 50 for interactive profile + evening batch at 200 RPS for summarization test.
- Models: Redwood-quantized variant, Redwood-fp16 variant, Hyperscaler baseline.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99, per-minute tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, 1-min/5-min latency histograms, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate from run logs.
- Batch policies: low-latency (max-batch 8, max-wait 8ms) and throughput (max-batch 64, max-wait 25ms).

Preliminary cost ballpark for the A/B run: 
- Redwood bench (24h steady + peaks): ~$1,200-1,800 (includes reserved bench infra and ephemeral GPUs)
- Hyperscaler: estimated $1,500-2,200 (depends on their managed endpoint IO and storage costs)

I can run the smoke test Thursday afternoon at 15:00 PDT. If that looks good, I’ll kick off the full A/B starting Friday 03:00 PDT for 36 hours to capture diurnal variance.

Attachments: globex_p95_p99_results.csv, latency_throughput_ab_test_results.pdf

2) During the full A/B, can you surface cost-per-1M-tokens as a separate column in the results CSV? Procurement will want that formatted for quick review.
3) For the smoke test on Thursday 15:00 PDT - please send a calendar invite and a short test-plan doc (one-pager). We’ll be online and will route any blocking errors to Max.
